chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ali ibn Uqba from one of our companions who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was with Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, the governor of Mecca, who was the husband of Fatimah bint Abi Abdillah. Muhammad ibn Ibrahim had a daughter whom he would dress in clothes, and she would come to the men; a man would take her and embrace her. When it reached Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), he held her with both hands extended and said: 'When a girl reaches six years of age, it is not permissible for a man who is not her mahram (close relative) to kiss her, nor to embrace her.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (Imam al-Hadi or Imam al-Hasan al-Askari, contextually the Imam)
key_terms.مَحْرَم: Close relative with whom marriage is permanently forbidden

ai.seo_question: At what age does it become impermissible for a non-mahram man to kiss or embrace a girl according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the age of six as the threshold for *hijab* and modesty, prohibiting non-mahram men from kissing or embracing young girls. It highlights the practical application of gender segregation principles in early Shia society, linking physical boundaries to the development of modesty (*hayā’*) in children. The ruling underscores the importance of protecting female dignity from an early age within the family and social structures.
